name: month-grid
title: Month calendar from nested loops
summary: A month calendar drawn by a week loop around a weekday loop: each cell's day number comes from the two indices and the month's first weekday, and step masks hide days outside the month, dim weekends and circle today.
prompt: Draw a month calendar for October 2026 (starts on a Thursday, 31 days) with Monday-first weekday initials, weekends dimmed and today, the 29th, circled.
teaches: Nest two loops (week 0..6, weekday 0..7) and turn the two indices into one value: day = week * 7 + wd + 1 - @firstWeekday
Name a per-iteration value with a variable command inside the loop body and reuse it in later commands of the same iteration
Hide, dim or show an item per iteration without a branch: a 0/1 step mask as paint alpha (inside the month, weekends) or as a radius (today's circle)
Drive a loop's content from exported variables, so the same document renders any month
pitfalls: step(a, b) is 1 only when a > b (strict): test day >= 1 as step(@day, 0.5) and day <= 31 as step(31.5, @day)

Avoid conditionalOperations inside a loop for anything that reads the loop index through an expression: a block updates all its commands' inputs before running them, so an expression computed in the block is one iteration late, and a value computed before the block may not refresh at all (C++). Masks keep it right
There is no break: a loop always runs from..until. Make the bounds cover the worst case (6 weeks) and mask the cells you do not want

Derive the cell pitch from componentWidth()/componentHeight() once (two variable commands before the loops) instead of literal 41 × 38 cells: the loop body reads @cw and @rh every iteration, and the weekday letters step along with translate(@cw), which costs no new expression

This grid is fixed to October 2026 to keep the loop lesson small (rc-inspect flags it: hardcoded_date). For 'this month' or 'today', compute the month, the weekday of the 1st, the day count and today from the clock, as TIM-10 does; never paste them.

snippets.note: outer loop over weeks, inner loop over weekdays
day number from both indices and @firstWeekday
paint alpha = inMonth, dimmed on weekdays 5 and 6

today.meaning: day of the month to circle (0 for none)

check.describe: October 2026: 1 under Thursday, 31 under Saturday, Saturday and Sunday columns dimmed, 29 in a blue circle; no numbers before the 1st or after the 31st. Resized (small 200×220, large 450×450) the grid spreads over the canvas: cells are cw = (componentWidth() - 13) / 7 wide and rh = (componentHeight() - 72) / 6 high, and today's circle is 0.42 × the smaller of the two.
